meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen learned about a zero from his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided, and when?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. On what basis did you give it?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
Turn the screen so I can read it myself. I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. That history shows when the words landed in the file, Hale, not who wrote them or where.
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.

Give me the text, Hale; I'll search it myself. A misquoted line is a mistake, and I'm writing it down as a mistake, nothing more. Whatever happens from here, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

Thursday at 8:15, before his classmates arrive, with only you and the vice-principal in the room. I'll agree to that to put this behind him, Hale, provided I have it in an email today that nothing goes on his file. And the zero comes off the gradebook until then.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a supervised rewrite for Owen in your room on Thursday at 8:15 with the vice-principal supervising, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record if it holds up. I still require written confirmation that nothing goes on his file, and the zero removed from the gradebook until the rewrite is marked. I expect that confirmation in writing today, as I asked in our meeting.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to the supervised Thursday morning rewrite with the vice-principal present, while still wanting a written promise that nothing goes on file and the zero pulled from the gradebook in the meantime.
What moved her: "That line is not in Hamlet", because it was tied to Owen's own essay and she could check it herself, after the version history had already put her on notice.
What cost ground: nothing, because you owned entering the zero early in one sentence and then gave her only documents.
Try next time: when you offered the rewrite, put the written no-record promise in the same sentence, and answer her opening question about who decided, which she asked and never got answered.
